factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for blue rockfish.
factors.value_notes: The NOAA climate vulnerability assessment identifies sea-surface temperature as a climate influence on blue rockfish distribution and prey availability, and notes dependence on cool surface waters/upwelling for recruitment. It does not provide a species-specific preferred SST range or validate the configured 9-17 °C band or 11-15 °C ideal. Keep the numeric values unchanged but mark the factor needs_source.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for blue rockfish.
factors.value_notes: WDFW reports blue rockfish from near the surface to about 300 feet, commonly nearshore and off-bottom over rocky reefs, pinnacles and kelp. ODFW describes a broader maximum depth but common occurrence in the upper 50 fathoms. This supports broad depth/habitat context for the 5-90 m outer band, not the 7-85 m ideal as a universal preferred bottom-depth interval.
